summary: Open a project on another connected SSH machine: the target clones the repository from the remote the current branch tracks (a fork, not the repository it was forked from), checks out the same branch under ~/projects, and lists the project at once. The desktop polls the clone, then copies only the ignored files the user picked (none by default; text, 1 MB each, no links, no install or build folders), reading each from the source backend and writing it to the target. A chat start in that project waits for the clone, and cached 'no favicon' and 'not a git repository' answers for the path are dropped when it ends.

reactNativeIos.reason: The phone app connects to one backend at a time and has no SSH machine list, so it cannot name a second machine to clone onto. The new project-clone channels need the terminal scope, which a paired phone never holds, so the phone cannot call them either. A project cloned from the desktop is an ordinary project row on the target and appears in the phone's project list through the existing app:get-projects read.

nativeAndroid.reason: Same as the React Native app: the native Android client talks to one backend, has no SSH machines to pick from, and holds only the chat scope, which the project-clone: prefix refuses. Cloned projects reach it through the existing project list read with no client change.

storageDataMigration.reason: No schema change. The clone adds one row to the target's existing projects table through addProject and removes it again if the clone fails. Clone progress is held in memory on the target and in the desktop renderer only; nothing new is persisted, so older and newer databases read each other unchanged.

updateRelease.reason: New backend capability project_clone_v1. The desktop checks it on the target before starting and shows 'too old to clone a project' for a target that lacks it, so a new desktop against an old headless server refuses cleanly. An old desktop never calls the channels. No package identity, signing, deep link or update channel change.

automated: tests/unit/project-clone-integration.test.ts runs real git against local bare repositories: a branch tracking a fork clones the fork and checks out that branch; a never-pushed branch falls back to the default branch; no remote answers no-remote; a failed clone removes the folder and the project row; unsafe URLs, folder names and branch names are refused; only an ignored, text, under-cap, non-link file is offered and read; the target writes it with mode 0600, never over an existing file and never a tracked path; a forgotten favicon cache entry lets a new icon through.

tests/unit/project-clone.test.ts pins the remote choice, the ignore-list filter, the text check, URL and folder-name checks, the progress line parser, and that a chat-scoped device cannot call project-clone channels.

tests/unit/project-clone-service.test.ts pins the desktop flow with a fake backend: it polls status, copies picked files source to target, reports files that failed, bumps the ready version that clears cached misses, resolves the send wait, and refuses a target without the capability.
notExercised: Not run against a real SSH machine or the packaged app. The dialog, the inline sidebar progress and the send wait were checked by typecheck and the service test only, not watched in the running app.

A clone that needs credentials the target does not have (an SSH host alias from the desktop's ssh config, or a private HTTPS remote) fails with git's message; that path is covered only by the failed-clone test.
A backend restart during a clone leaves the half clone and its project row in place and answers status unknown; the desktop then reports that the machine lost track of the clone.
